chapter: Probation, Las Vegas and Los Angeles in the 1950s
title: The Clark Hotel and its rehearsal band
summary: The Clark's back room let jazz players blow steam off; he lived there in 1962 with Louis Bellson.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Well, then, after they closed the Moulin Rouge down they opened another hotel, the Clark Hotel. And they had a setup for music, but they didn't have a casino or anything like that. Just had a bar, you know, and a bandstand. And the back room was a larger room with a larger bandstand, and they used that for rehearsal band purposes mostly. You know, the jazz musicians that was working on the strip in the main room didn't get a chance to play jazz, so they'd come over there and sit in with the rehearsal band, in order to blow steam off, you know. And then some of them was just learning to arrange, and they was bringing in arrangements, 'Play this,' you know, so we were pretty well occupied after they built the
I was down there in '62 with Louis Bellson. That's where Harold Land and I stopped. We had adjoining rooms, you know.
Was that when it opened? The Clark opened in '62?
No, it was open before that, but I had occasion to live there in '62.
Do you know when it opened?
